segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Miss Tan. I'm Dr. Liew, the anesthesiologist who'll be taking care of you during your surgery today. I just need to go through a few questions to make sure everything goes smoothly for your laparoscopic ovarian cystectomy. Is that okay with you?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, doctor. I'm ready. Been waiting for this for weeks already lah.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. Let's start with your medical history. Can you tell me a bit about the ovarian cyst? When did you first notice symptoms?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: About three months ago, I had really bad lower tummy pain, like cramps but worse. My gynae did an ultrasound and found the cyst. They said it's about 6cm, so they want to remove it before it gets bigger or causes more trouble.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understood. Now, let's go through your medications. You're on amlodipine for your blood pressure, right? What dose are you taking?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, amlodipine 5mg once daily in the morning. And my birth control pills, levonorgestrel and ethinyl estradiol, same time every day. Oh, and I stopped doxycycline two weeks ago because of the surgery.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you. Now, about allergies – your records say 'no known allergies,' but I always like to double-check. Have you ever had a reaction to any antibiotics, particularly sulfa-based medications like co-trimoxazole or sulfadiazine?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Oh! Actually, yes. When I was a teenager, I took some sulfa pills for a skin infection and broke out in a terrible rash all over my body. It was really scary. I've avoided all sulfa drugs since then.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for sharing that. I'll make sure to note your sulfa allergy clearly in your chart. Now, have you eaten or drunk anything since midnight? We need to confirm your NPO status for general anesthesia.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, doctor. I had my last sip of water at 7am. Just like the instructions said.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. Any previous surgeries or anesthesia? Even minor procedures like stitching or dental work?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, this is my first time. I'm a bit nervous about the general anesthesia, to be honest.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: It's normal to feel that way. Finally, can you tell me about your daily activities? For example, can you walk up stairs or carry groceries without getting short of breath?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, I walk to work every day and climb five flights of stairs. No problems at all. I'm quite active, lah.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's reassuring. We'll make sure your blood pressure is well-controlled during surgery since you're on amlodipine. Any other concerns before we proceed?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I think that's all. Thank you for explaining everything so clearly, doctor.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: My pleasure, Miss Tan. We'll take good care of you. The nursing team will come for you shortly. See you in the operating theater.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:02] tube in, grade one view

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] 16-gauge line placed in right antecubital vein

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] crystalloid two thousand milliliters administered

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:30] blood pressure dropped to 85 over 50, gave ephedrine ten milligrams IV

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [09:15] blood pressure up to 160 over 90, gave labetalol twenty milligrams IV

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi there, how are you feeling now after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Eh, still a bit tired, but okay lah. Got some pain here, like a deep ache, but not too bad.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understandable. Can you rate your pain for me, out of 10?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Maybe 3 or 4? The nurse already gave me some meds, so it's better now.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Any nausea or vomiting since waking up? Sometimes the anesthesia can cause that.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: A bit dizzy earlier, but no vomiting. Felt like my stomach was churning, but it's gone now.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Okay. How's your breathing? Any tightness or discomfort in your throat from the tube?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Throat is a bit sore, like I swallowed something big, but I can breathe fine. No wheezing or anything.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good to hear. Do you remember anything about the surgery itself?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Nope, everything's a blank. Just woke up here, so I guess the anesthesia worked well.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect. Since you have hypertension, we've been monitoring your BP. It's been stable, but we'll keep an eye on it.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Okay, thanks. I was worried it might spike, but I feel okay now.

Intraoperatively, propofol was administered, followed by uneventful intubation. A 16-gauge IV was placed, and 2000mL crystalloid was given. Blood pressure fluctuated, requiring ephedrine for hypotension and labetalol for hypertension.

Anticipated issues include hemodynamic instability due to intraoperative BP fluctuations and pre-existing hypertension, post-operative nausea and vomiting risk given female gender, laparoscopic surgery, and possible opioid use, and sulfa allergy requiring avoidance of sulfa-based medications.
Monitor for hemodynamic instability, manage BP as needed. Administer antiemetics for PONV prophylaxis. Avoid sulfa-based medications due to allergy.
